title.narrative: Laos Supporting coffee farmers in northern Laos

description.narrative: Under the guidance of UPLAO, this project aims to create sustainable alternatives for ever expanding monocropping agriculture in the uplands of northern Laos. Upland farmers in this region traditionally have limited options to make cash for a living and mostly rely on the cultivation rubber which yields low prices and has a detrimental impact on the natural environment. The cultivation of rubber implies clear cutting of forests and through excessive use of chemicals, soils are depleted and watershed systems are polluted. This poses a threat to local ecosystems leaving local communities vulnerable to maintain their livelihoods. Over the past 3 years UPLAO been promoting shade-grown organic coffee cultivation as a high value and sustainable alternative for upland communities in the region. Besides providing farmers with sustainable livelihoods and at the same time combat ecological degradation as the coffee is grown in agroforestry settings. There are now over 70 households that have chosen to to convert to agroforestry coffee production and this project will help to further support these households to facilitate the success of this green conversion. For this a team of 5 technical field officers will be trained in all aspects of organic coffee cultivation. For two years they will lead all 70 households to a successful transition to organic agriculture and a first harvest of high-quality organic shade-grown coffee arabica. Ultimately this project will contribute to deliver this coffee to consumers in the west. Coffee that’s traceably not detrimental to the local society nor the ecosystem.
